C0.quote: We analyse optimal voting weights in two-tier voting systems.
C0.note: Weighted council voting aggregating group majorities.

C1.quote: minimise the democracy deficit, i.e. the expected deviation of the council
C1.note: Most main results compute weights that minimise the democracy deficit (WD). The paper also proposes the generalised CBM and proves its large-population limit behaviour (Theorem 15), which is a modelling proposal and probability result (OT).

C5.1.quote: a measure of how well the council votes follow the public opinion
C5.1.note: The democracy deficit, used in all results, measures representation of the population's vote.

C5.2.quote: deviation of the council vote from a hypothetical referendum
C5.2.note: The deficit is evaluated on submitted votes S. The paper states that votes obey preferences.

VOT.note: Includes individual voters (votes drawn from the CBM) and council representatives (follow the group majority).

C9.2.quote: obeying the voters’ preferences which we do not model explicitly
C9.2.note: The needed assumptions are stated: votes obey preferences, and representatives vote with the group majority. That the bias model approximates reality is a general modelling assumption and is excluded by the codebook.

C1.reason: The conclusion lists defining the generalised CBM and its asymptotic behaviour (Theorem 15) as main findings, so OT applies alongside the primary WD results.

C9.2.reason: The assumptions the claims need are stated in Section 1, and B's unstated items are either general model-realism or normative choices, which do not count as needed assumptions.
